name: MIT Cheetah 3
def: Forty kilogram electric quadruped that climbed cluttered stairs and jumped onto tables using only proprioception, with no cameras.
body: Cheetah 3 kept the proprioceptive actuators of the earlier Cheetah machines and added greater joint range and a stiffer frame. Two algorithms did the work: a contact detection routine that decided when each foot had truly touched down, and a model predictive controller that recomputed leg forces every fifty milliseconds. Working blind from gyroscopes, accelerometers and joint sensors alone, it climbed a debris strewn staircase and leapt onto a desk about seventy six centimetres high.
facts: Climbed stairs littered with obstacles with no vision at all
Its control software became the basis of the open source stack used on Mini Cheetah
specs: Proprioceptive brushless motors with low gear ratio transmissions
Inertial measurement unit and joint encoders only
Model predictive control with contact detection and no exteroceptive sensing
